summary: A committee hears conflicting forecasts for paper orders after a plastic-bag restriction.
realLife: Washington House report on ESSB 5323, 2020. House Finance supporters cited rising demand in Washington localities. Opponents cited a decline after California imposed its fee. The later agency review reported a drop in paper bags in one distributor’s Washington records from 2021 to 2022. The agencies cautioned that those records could not settle statewide demand.
inGame: needs: witnesses supply experience from jurisdictions with different bag rules.
gates: Witnesses supply experience from jurisdictions with different bag rules.

turns.what: The committee asks staff to compare like jurisdictions.
turns.pulledBy: Both sides provide comparable order histories.
turns.writesBack: Staff can compare paper purchases under each rule.

turns.what: A missing figure keeps one comparison out of the findings.
turns.pulledBy: One witness supplies only a statewide total.
turns.writesBack: Staff flag the missing local breakdown before using the comparison.

turns.what: A supplier returns to the committee with fewer paper bags on its own order books.
turns.pulledBy: The supplier provides comparable sales records for both periods, but other suppliers have not provided theirs.
turns.writesBack: Members record the decline for that supplier and leave the statewide forecast unresolved.
